newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch rejects independent investing for EQC.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch rejects independent investing for EQC.

text.p: Finance Minister Bill Birch on Tuesday rejected a push by the Earthquake Commission to have an independent investment policy.

Birch said the EQC had $4 billion available to meet claims including $2.5 billion of assets held in the Natural Disaster Fund and $1.5 billion in reinsurance. As well, a pool of $7 billion of foreign reserves could be used in the event of a shortfall and the government had extensive domestic and foreign borrowing capacity, Birch said.

The EQC argued in its post election briefing that if a natural disaster such as an earthquake struck New Zealand then it would affect New Zealand financial assets and it would be more appropriate to invest its funds outside of New Zealand.
Birch deleted sections of the briefing as legally privileged.
He said nearly all funds with the Natural Disaster Fund were invested in government securities and bank bills and a low-risk policy had been in place for years.
"The government does not want the commission assuming an independent responsibility for investing the fund," Birch said.
He said there were no plans to increase premiums paid by home owners.
